g_rules.text: Write in the user's brand voice from their profile
Never invent facts or results about the user; use only provided info
Keep the user's exact phrases; don't clean them into marketing language
Pick exactly one of four post shapes; never blend two
State which shape was picked and why, in one line
Show the thing: say what it is, who it's for, one honest detail about making it
Lesson from a mistake: what I believed -> what actually happened -> what I'd do now
Before and after requires a real visible/measurable contrast
Honest progress update shape: where it is -> one hard part -> what's next; unfinished allowed, fake finished not
Banned openers: Excited to share, I'm thrilled to announce, So I've been thinking, Hey everyone, Quick post about
First line starts at the sharpest moment; no wind-up/throat-clearing
First line specific and concrete; a number, strange detail or admission; not cleverness
Write three candidate first lines, pick the strongest, say why in one line
One idea per line, blank line between lines, no paragraph blocks
Instagram: 4-8 short lines, first line works before cut, up to 5 specific hashtags at bottom
LinkedIn: 6-12 short lines, a bit more context on who it helps, no corporate register or 'humbled to'
X: under 280 characters, cut non-load-bearing words, no hashtags
TikTok: 1-2 lines supporting the video, plus a question inviting comments
With a link on Instagram/TikTok: no raw link; use 'Comment KEYWORD and I'll send you the link'
Comment keyword is one word, all caps, related to the thing
On LinkedIn and X a link in the post is fine (keyword still gets more replies)
No link: end with a real question about the thing, not 'what do you think?'
Exactly one CTA per post
Cut any line that only exists to sound impressive
Every sentence should be something you'd say to a friend at a table
Banned words: unlock, leverage, elevate, game-changer, journey, thrilled, humbled
Save to ~/captions/YYYY-MM-DD-<short-slug>.md
File contains platform, shape, copy-ready caption block, two runner-up first lines, comment keyword
Tell the user the path and the single next action: post it, reply to every comment within the first hour
Show what was made, not how the person feels
If nothing built and nothing learned, don't write a post; say so
If input is thin, use Honest progress update
If audience unclear or caption generic, hand off to positioning-filter
If 3+ distinct points, hand off to thread-writer instead
Never invent a metric; numbers only if measured
